text:
morgan: Quick Q — we're finalizing the prompt caching contract for the API. Need clarity on which response-level signals we guarantee for backcompat: `x-cache-hit`, `cache-control`, and any JSON body `cache` object. Also: should invalidation events clear both prefix and full-key entries?
ryan: short answer: keep `x-cache-hit` stable. consumers already parse it. prefer header + body field for richer info.
jia: +1 to stable header. can we standardize values? e.g. `x-cache-hit: miss|hit|stale` so it's machineable.
samir: agree on enum. also: we need a clear rule for streaming responses — header arrives early but body `cache` object may be populated after stream end. that will break some clients.
morgan: good call. for streaming we can include the header upfront and append a small `cache-summary` event at end-of-stream. something like: `event: cache-summary\ndata: {"hit":"hit","key":"pfx:abcd...","reason":"prefix-match"}`
nora: Reaction: :thumbsup: on `miss|hit|stale`. For headers vs `cache-control` I prefer not to overload `cache-control` — it's used by proxies and browsers. Keep our signals separate.
ryan: Agreed. `cache-control` should remain HTTP semantics. use `x-rw-cache` or `x-cache-hit`. Also we should include `x-cache-key` only when it's safe to expose (redaction/privacy).
morgan: Proposal (RFC):
```
HTTP response headers:
  x-cache-hit: hit|miss|stale
  x-cache-key: <short-key-or-omitted>
  x-cache-variant: prefix|exact

Body addition (optional):
  "cache": {"hit": "hit", "key": "pfx:abcd1234", "variant": "prefix"}
```
Clients can rely on `x-cache-hit` for immediate routing; body `cache` is advisory.
jia: minor nit: prefer `x-cache-variant: prefix|exact|partial`? partial for partial-match cases.
samir: Also need to define invalidation semantics: if we invalidate a prefix, should we mark exact-key entries as invalid too? I think yes — prefix invalidation must clear exact and prefix entries that start with that prefix. Document as atomic operation.
morgan: Draft wording: "Prefix invalidation removes any cache entries whose key has the prefix. Exact invalidation removes only the exact key." simple. add TTL interplay note.
ryan: Backcompat concern: old clients might only look for `X-Cache-Hit` case-insensitive. publish both canonical lower-case headers and also allow legacy `X-Cache-Hit`? HTTP is case-insensitive but some libs are picky. I'd rather emit both `x-cache-hit` and `X-Cache-Hit` for a short transition window.
nora: hmm we can't send duplicates with different casing; many servers normalize. let's document header name exactly and add a middleware shim in the SDKs to normalize.
infra-bot: CI check: `cache-schema.json` validation failed in branch `feature/cache-signals` — missing `variant` enum entry. https://ci.internal/5678
morgan: thanks infra-bot — I'll fix the schema.
ryan: Quick question on invalidation API: do we expose `POST /v1/cache/invalidate` with body `{"prefix":"pfx:"}` or prefer `DELETE /v1/cache/pfx%3A...`?
jia: POST is easier for async (returns job id) and can accept lists. prefer POST with optional `wait=true` query param.
samir: make sure invalidation is idempotent and returns list of affected shards for ops. useful for troubleshooting.
morgan: action items: 1) I'll update the open RFC with header names + enums + streaming event note. 2) Jia to add POST invalidation proposal + examples. 3) Ryan to add SDK shim for header normalization. 4) Samir to add invalidation atomicity tests.
nora: ping me when RFC is updated — I'll check privacy implications for `x-cache-key` exposure.
deploy-bot: Deployment note: rolling out `cache-signals-v2` to canary cluster at 2026-03-18T03:00Z. watch `cache.hit.rate` metric.
morgan: thanks — I'll hold the rollout if schema isn't updated.
ryan: I pushed a tiny PR that adds `stale` to the enum and documents streaming `cache-summary` event. link: https://git.redwood/r/redwood-inference/p/cache-signals/pull/42
jia: LGTM, left one comment about max key length for `x-cache-key` (suggest 64 chars).
samir: we'll also need a migration note for Dedicated customers that rely on `cache-control` today. ops should send a heads-up.
morgan: wrapping up: we'll consider header canonicalization via SDKs, keep `cache` body optional, use POST invalidation with job ids, and make prefix invalidation clear all matching entries. will circulate updated RFC by EOD PST. thanks all!
